chunks: Yet We know what they say: 'It is only a man who instructs him.' The speech of the man they imply is obscure while this is clear Arabic.
ai.seo_question: Who is the 'man' referred to in Surah An-Nahl verse 103?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to highlight the miraculous nature of the Quran's eloquence (balagha), proving it could not be the work of a human, especially one who spoke a non-Arabic dialect. The reference to 'Ajam' (foreigners) specifically points to Abdallah ibn Harithah, a companion of the Prophet known for his fluency in Arabic but not as the source of the Quran's linguistic miracle. This refutation underscores the divine origin of the text, a key tenet in Shia theology regarding the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Quran.
